question: A container holds a mixture of Orange, Apple, and Guava juices in the ratio of 5:7:4 respectively. 24 litres of this mixture is taken out, and then 10 litres of orange juice and 6 litres of guava juice are added to the vessel. If the resultant quantity of apple juice is 14 litres more than the resultant quantity of orange juice, what was the initial quantity of mixture in the vessel (in litres)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial mixture be 16x. The initial parts are Orange = 5x, Apple = 7x.

Removing 24 litres takes out (5 / 16) × 24 = 7.5L Orange and (7 / 16) × 24 = 10.5L Apple.

Resultant Apple − Resultant Orange = (7x − 10.5) − (5x − 7.5 + 10) = 14.

⇒ 2x − 13 = 14 ⇒ 2x = 27.

Initial quantity = 16x = 27 × 8 = 216.

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Orange : Apple : Guava = 5 : 7 : 4

Quantity of mixture taken out = 24 litres

Quantity of added juices = 10 litres Orange, 6 litres Guava

Resultant Apple juice − Resultant Orange juice = 14 litres

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total ratio parts initially = 5 + 7 + 4 = 16 parts

⇒ Let the initial quantity of mixture be 16x litres.

⇒ The initial quantities are Orange = 5x, Apple = 7x, and Guava = 4x.

⇒ Quantity of Orange juice removed = (5 / 16) × 24 = 7.5 litres

⇒ Quantity of Apple juice removed = (7 / 16) × 24 = 10.5 litres

After taking out 24 litres and adding the respective juices, the new volumes are:

⇒ Resultant Orange juice = 5x − 7.5 + 10 = 5x + 2.5

⇒ Resultant Apple juice = 7x − 10.5

According to the given condition, the difference is 14 litres:

⇒ (7x − 10.5) − (5x + 2.5) = 14

⇒ 7x − 10.5 − 5x − 2.5 = 14

⇒ 2x − 13 = 14

⇒ 2x = 27

⇒ x = 13.5

⇒ Initial quantity of mixture = 16x = 16 × 13.5 = 216 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Ratio Property

When any volume of a mixture is drawn out, the remaining mixture still contains the original ingredients in the exact same ratio. Only adding or removing an individual component selectively will alter this final ratio.

Replacement Method

When a certain volume of mixture is replaced completely by one of its pure ingredients, the remaining quantity of the pure liquid left can be found using the formula: Final = Initial × (1 − Removed/Total)ⁿ.

Rule of Alligation

Used to find the required ratio when two ingredients at different prices or concentrations are mixed. Ratio = (Dearer − Mean) : (Mean − Cheaper).
